decisions.notes: The packet flagged quote_mismatch=true on the Rapid City Journal source; I decoded the article's ROT47-obfuscated paywall HTML (Lee Enterprises/BLOX CMS 'encrypted-content' divs -- confirmed present in the archived .html) and the decoded text matches the cited quote and full embedded timeline verbatim, including 'Oct. 21, 2025: Commission votes unanimously to extend the moratorium to Nov. 18, 2026.' This is a false-positive quote_mismatch caused by paywall encoding, not a fabrication. I further pulled the actual Oct. 21, 2025 Pennington County Board of Commissioners minutes (primary source, newly archived this pass) and confirmed the extension vote directly: the item was 'EXTENSION OF ORDINANCE #741 ... effective upon completed publication (November 06, 2025)'; a substitute motion to change 'the date provided by the State's Attorney's Office of November 18th' to 'February 18, 2026' FAILED 2-3, and the original motion (keeping November 18) passed unanimously. This resolves an apparent conflict with a separate stale draft ordinance PDF on the county's own site (docs.pennco.org/.../Ordinance741Ext.pdf) that reads 'shall expire on February 17, 2026' -- that PDF appears to be an earlier draft superseded by the meeting's amendments, not the adopted text. Row's extension-to-Nov.-18-2026 claim is correct. The Aug. 18, 2026 permanent zoning ban on agricultural land is confirmed as a separate, legally distinct action (also decoded from the same ROT47 archive) that does not itself rescind the moratorium.

decisions.notes: The underlying August 2025 ordinance ('Moratorium on Solar and Wind Energy Systems') is real and is a genuine temporary pause, not a permanent ban -- confirmed by Board of Adjustment minutes referencing 'the County Commissioner's adoption of the ordinance.' But it was reported as a *one-year* moratorium enacted 'on or about August 2025,' which would lapse around August 2026 unless renewed. A public notice indicated a hearing was set for Aug. 25, 2026 specifically 'to consider extending' it -- consistent with the county itself recognizing the natural end was approaching. I made further attempts (beyond the original researcher's) to find the outcome of that Aug. 25, 2026 hearing: the notice-registry page has no retained notice text (confirmed, JS-rendered boilerplate only), the Turner County Board of Adjustment's own site only indexes Board-of-Adjustment (not County Commission) agendas/minutes, and a mytownview.com page for the relevant County Commission meeting date rendered empty (JS-only). I could not locate the Commission's actual Aug. 25, 2026 vote or any confirmation the ordinance was renewed. Given the one-year term and the lapse risk, 'active' as of 2026-09-23 cannot be confirmed one way or the other; this should be treated as materially uncertain rather than confirmed. Recommend a follow-up pass once Turner County posts its Aug./Sept. 2026 County Commission minutes.
